topics.label: Ecosystems
facts: An ecosystem is a community of living things and the non-living things around them, all interacting.
Producers, consumers, and decomposers all play roles in an ecosystem.
Decomposers, like fungi and bacteria, break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil.
A food web is a set of linked food chains that shows how feeding relationships connect in an ecosystem.

choices: A community of living things and their surroundings, all interacting
questions.fact: An ecosystem includes everything living and non-living in an area and how they affect each other.

choices: Break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil
questions.fact: Fungi and bacteria decompose dead matter, recycling nutrients for new life.

choices: Linked food chains showing how feeding relationships connect
questions.fact: A food web joins many food chains together, showing that most animals eat more than one thing.

questions.q: In an ecosystem, what do we call animals that eat plants and animals?
questions.fact: Omnivores eat both plants and other animals.

topics.label: Climate
facts: Climate is the usual pattern of weather in a place over a long time, while weather is what happens day to day.
Earth's climate is warming because greenhouse gases, like carbon dioxide, trap heat in the atmosphere.
Burning coal, oil, and gas releases carbon dioxide into the air.
Melting ice and rising sea levels are signs that Earth's climate is changing.

questions.q: What is the difference between weather and climate?
choices: Weather is day to day; climate is the usual pattern over a long time
Weather is only rain; climate is only heat
questions.fact: Weather is short-term, while climate describes the usual weather of a place over many years.

questions.q: Which gas is the main greenhouse gas warming Earth's climate?
questions.fact: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere, warming the planet.

questions.q: What releases carbon dioxide into the air?
questions.fact: Burning fossil fuels for energy releases stored carbon as carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Which of these is a sign that Earth's climate is changing?
choices: Melting ice and rising sea levels
questions.fact: As the planet warms, glaciers melt and the seas rise.

topics.label: The Carbon Cycle
facts: The carbon cycle is the movement of carbon between the air, living things, the oceans, and rocks.
Plants take carbon dioxide out of the air during photosynthesis and store the carbon in their bodies.
Animals get carbon by eating plants or other animals, and release carbon dioxide when they breathe out.
Burning fossil fuels moves carbon that was stored underground for millions of years into the air very quickly.

choices: The movement of carbon between the air, living things, oceans, and rocks
questions.fact: Carbon moves around the planet in a cycle, from air to living things and back again.

questions.q: How do plants take carbon out of the air?
questions.fact: In photosynthesis, plants take in carbon dioxide and use its carbon to grow.

questions.q: How do animals release carbon dioxide?
questions.fact: Respiration releases carbon dioxide back into the air.

questions.q: Why does burning fossil fuels add carbon dioxide to the air quickly?
choices: It releases carbon stored underground for millions of years
questions.fact: Coal, oil, and gas hold carbon from ancient living things, and burning them frees it as carbon dioxide.

topics.label: Biodiversity
facts: Biodiversity means the variety of all living things on Earth, from tiny bacteria to huge whales.
Rainforests and coral reefs have some of the highest biodiversity on the planet.
When a species becomes extinct, it is gone forever, and the food web it belonged to can weaken.
Protecting habitats is the most important way to protect biodiversity.

choices: The variety of all living things on Earth
questions.fact: Biodiversity is the variety of life, including all species and ecosystems.

questions.q: Which places have some of the highest biodiversity?
questions.fact: Rainforests and coral reefs support a huge number of different species.

questions.q: What happens when a species becomes extinct?
choices: It comes back after a year
It turns into a different species
questions.fact: Extinction is permanent: once a species is gone, it never returns.

questions.q: What is the most important way to protect biodiversity?
questions.fact: Protecting habitats keeps the places species need to live and survive.
